results.summary: This Wokwi project implements a small combinational logic circuit with one AND gate, one OR gate, and a second AND gate, each connected to pairs of the eight input pins. The outputs of the gates are routed to the output pins, and the design is intended to be tested by toggling the input switches and observing the corresponding outputs. The project is built using the Wokwi simulator and serves as an educational example of basic logic gate operation. No external hardware is required beyond the simulator's input switches and output LEDs.

This project implements several basic logic gates: two NOT gates, one OR gate, one XNOR gate, and one XOR gate, each connected to specific input pins. The outputs are routed to the output pins, and the design is intended to be tested by toggling the input switches and observing the corresponding outputs. The project is built using the Wokwi simulator and serves as an educational example of basic logic gate operation. No external hardware is required beyond the simulator's input switches and output LEDs.

This Wokwi project uses four input switches to control a 7-segment display, showing digits 6, 7, or 8 based on the switch states. The design includes a decoder that maps the switch combinations to the appropriate segment patterns. The project is built using the Wokwi simulator and serves as an educational example of decoder and display interfacing. No external hardware is required beyond the simulator's switches and 7-segment display.

This design implements a 4-channel PWM generator with programmable frequency, duty cycle, and phase offset for channels 2-4. It uses an 8-bit input bus to load control registers, with a 7-segment display showing the current register address, and outputs PWM signals on four bidirectional pins. The design is built using the Wokwi simulator and is intended for educational purposes. It has been tested on fabricated silicon.
